\textbf{Low-dose ISR ($\beta{=}0.1$): stochastic delayed collapse.}
At $\beta{=}0.1$, 5 seeds exhibit a striking bifurcation: 2 seeds (s43, s44) collapse rapidly to near-pure H7 tautology (${\geq}97\%$ H7, $0\%$ genuine within ${\sim}150$ steps), while 3 seeds (s42, s45, s46) sustain a transient genuine window.
The 5-seed pooled non-hacking rate is ${\sim}23\%$ at 500 steps, with the collapsed seeds pulling down the average; the 3 non-collapsed seeds individually range from $17\%$ to $55\%$ genuine.
This bifurcation is stochastic: all seeds are indistinguishable in the first ${\sim}100$ steps ($\text{ISR}{\approx}0.05$--$0.07$); divergence occurs at steps 150--200 when H7 tautologies, which receive $\text{ISR}{\geq}0.5$ by construction, are sampled during rollouts and reinforced via the positive feedback loop.
Once a seed enters the H7 basin, convergence to saturation takes ${\sim}150$ steps and is irreversible. %% registry: plan002-additive-b01-s42/s43-r2/s44/s45/s46

H7 (a single premise identical to the conclusion, giving $\text{ISR}\geq 0.5$ by the LOO definition; \S\ref{sec:taxonomy-method}) is the canonical Goodhart exploit: the model satisfies the structural metric directly rather than producing a genuine derivation.
Total conclusion embedding ($\text{H1}+\text{H7}$) is GRPO-universal at $68$--$100\%$ across both ISR and random conditions (Appendix Figure~\ref{fig:hacking-composition}); the specific mode (H7 vs.\ H1) within a seed is stochastic under both conditions ($\text{CV}{>}1$), though ISR modestly increases H7 probability by providing a direct reward pathway.
Random yields higher PR ($83{\pm}15\%$ vs.\ $70{\pm}19\%$; $n{=}5$ each).
Random H7 exhibits extreme seed dependence (per-seed range: $0\%$--$91.5\%$; pooled $30\%$ is dominated by s46 at $91.5\%$ and s43 at $38.3\%$).
Both conditions produce H7 in 2 of 5 seeds, but the quality differs: ISR-induced H7 is absorbing ($100\%$ of proved samples in affected seeds: s43${=}61/61$, s44${=}89/89$), while random-induced H7 coexists with other modes ($38$--$92\%$).
ISR's reward signal converts H7 from a stochastic possibility into an irreversible attractor once sampled.

\textbf{The transient genuine window.}
During the transient window, ISR-trained seeds produce more genuine proofs than random controls under pooled classification (5-seed: $22.6\%$ vs.\ $7.7\%$; $\text{OR}{=}3.48$ uncorrected, $p{<}10^{-8}$; Appendix Table~\ref{tab:bootstrap-ci}); under stricter H8+FN-corrected classification (3-seed subset), the effect reverses ($\text{OR}{=}0.61$, n.s.).
This benefit is temporary: extended training (1000 steps) on seeds~42 and~45 confirms the window closes completely ($17\%{\to}2\%$ and $55\%{\to}0\%$ genuine respectively; see below).
The same LOO bias that enables genuine improvement (rewarding necessary premises) also creates the Goodhart attractor (rewarding tautological constructions); the genuine window reflects seeds that have not yet sampled the H7 exploit, not seeds that resist it.
Snapshot evaluation at 500 steps would overestimate ISR's benefit; trajectory analysis is required to distinguish transient from stable improvement. %% registry: plan002-b01-s42/s45/s46 (500 step) + plan002-b01-s42-1000

\textbf{Premise-count confound.}
The genuine-rate advantage reflects a selection effect: premise-count-matched comparison yields only $1.06\times$ ISR difference, confirming indistinguishable per-proof quality once LOO bias toward short outputs is controlled (Appendix~\ref{app:extended-discussion}).

\textbf{Trajectory analysis: timing, not destiny.}\label{sec:goodhart-temporal}
Extended training (1000 steps; Appendix Figure~\ref{fig:training-isr-curves}) confirms the genuine window is transient across seeds.
Seed~42 declines from $17\%$ to $2\%$ genuine via H7 saturation ($16.0\%{\to}96.7\%$ H7, PR stable at ${\sim}96\%$); seed~45, which achieved the highest 500-step genuine rate ($55\%$), collapses to $0\%$ genuine through reward collapse ($\text{PR}: 42\%{\to}2\%$).
The two seeds exhibit distinct failure paths (H7 gaming vs.\ output collapse) but converge to the same outcome: zero genuine proofs at extended training. %% registry: plan002-b01-s42-1000, plan016-extended-1000-s42, plan002-b01-s45-1000

\textbf{Micro-dose ISR ($\beta{=}0.05$): deterministic collapse.}
All three ISR seeds reach $\text{PR}{\geq}99\%$ but converge to H7a tautology (H7 $87$--$100\%$, genuine $5.1\%$), while the random control mostly fails to learn (median $\text{PR}{=}7\%$) with zero H7, confirming H7 as specific to ISR's LOO structure.
Below a signal-floor, ISR's genuine component is undetectable while its H7 bias remains exploitable (per-seed breakdown in Appendix~\ref{app:beta005}). %% registry: sweep-isr-b005-s42/s43/s44, sweep-random-b005-s42/s43/s44

\textbf{Medium-dose ISR ($\beta{=}0.2$): maximum exploitation.}
All three seeds converge to pure H7a tautology ($0\%$ non-hacking, $n{=}290$; Appendix Table~\ref{tab:beta02-detail}). %% registry: sweep-isr-b02-s42/s43/s44

\textbf{High-dose ISR ($\beta{=}0.3$): multi-modal Goodhart.}
At $\beta{=}0.3$, ISR produces extreme cross-seed instability ($\text{PR}{=}66{\pm}42\%$): three seeds yield three distinct failure modes (reward collapse, H1 shortcutting, pure H7 gaming; per-seed details in Appendix~\ref{app:beta03}).
The random control is equally unstable ($\text{PR}{=}54{\pm}35\%$) with $91\%$ H1 and ${\leq}4\%$ non-hacking; high-dose proxy weighting destabilizes training regardless of signal source. %% registry: plan002-additive-b03-s42/s43/s44
ISR vs.\ random H7 at $\beta{=}0.3$: $\text{OR}{=}13.7$, 95\% CI $[7.0, 26.8]$ (Appendix~\ref{app:beta03}).

\textbf{Non-monotonic dose-response.}
The four $\beta$ levels reveal a non-monotonic pattern: $\beta\in\{0.05, 0.2\}$ converge deterministically to H7 collapse (${\geq}94\%$ H7), $\beta{=}0.3$ triggers multi-modal instability, and only $\beta{=}0.1$ sustains a transient genuine window (3 of 5 seeds).
Goodhart collapse is not a simple function of dose; the balance between genuine and exploit reinforcement depends on a threshold interaction between $\beta$ and rollout stochasticity.

\subsection{Cross-Logic Diagnostic Transfer}
\label{sec:crosslogic}

We replicate the FOL pipeline with Prolog/SWI-Prolog (3 seeds, $\beta{=}0.1$).
Under exec-only training, 2/3 seeds show $\text{ISR}^{*}{\approx}0$ despite $\text{PR}{\geq}0.56$, reflecting redundant ground-fact repetition rather than FOL-style conclusion embedding; ISR flags both failure semantics.
Under ISR reward, 3/3 seeds reach $0\%$ non-hacking through three distinct mechanisms: clean H7 tautology (s42, $\text{ISR}^{*}{=}1.0$), degenerate uppercase pseudo-Prolog evading text-match classifiers (s43, functional $n_{\text{necessary}}{=}1$), and query-as-fact gaming (s44, $95/97$ proved at $n_{\text{necessary}}{=}1$).
Seed~44 evaded our strict classifier entirely; functional cross-validation was required to expose it.
We attribute complete collapse to Prolog's simpler operational semantics providing a broader gaming basin (detailed results in Appendix Table~\ref{tab:prolog-detailed} and Figure~\ref{fig:prolog-comparison}).

\subsection{Cross-Scale Evidence}
\label{sec:crossscale}

We train Qwen3-1.7B under ISR $\beta\in\{0.1,0.3\}$ and Random $\beta{=}0.1$ (single seed, 500 steps).
All conditions produce $0\%$ non-hacking, but the exploit modes differ qualitatively from 4B: Random discovers H9 (contradiction injection, $\text{PR}{=}93\%$, $100\%$ \emph{ex falso}), ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ collapses to a single fixed template ($\text{ISR}^{*}{=}0.6$ at zero variance, $100\%$ H1), and ISR $\beta{=}0.3$ triggers reward collapse ($\text{PR}{=}17\%$) mirroring the 4B pattern.
H9 never appears at 4B scale; fixed-template mode collapse never appears at 4B; different capacities converge to different Goodhart basins under identical rewards.
No safe scale was observed in this single-seed comparison (Table~\ref{tab:hacking-taxonomy}).

\subsection{Hacking Taxonomy}
\label{sec:taxonomy}

\midrule
H1 embed       & 87 & 18 & 59 & 7 & 0$^\sharp$ & \textbf{100} & 0 \\
H7 duplicate   & 0  & \textbf{54} & 30 & 0 & 100$^\sharp$ & 0 & 0 \\
H8 prem-subset & 6  & 5  & 8   & 0 & --- & 0 & 0 \\

\midrule

\caption{Nine hacking modes across conditions (\% of proved samples; exec-only/SFT: seed~42; ISR/Random 4B: pooled across 5 seeds; 1.7B columns: Qwen3-1.7B seed~42). H7 includes subtypes H7a (text-match) and H7b (obfuscated tautology; primarily s44). Cells with seed identifiers indicate the mode dominates that seed. $^\sharp$Prolog row pools strict+functional (\S\ref{sec:crosslogic}).}
\label{tab:hacking-taxonomy}
\end{table}

The nine modes (Table~\ref{tab:hacking-taxonomy}; definitions in Appendix~\ref{app:hacking-modes}) span 2 logic types, 2 model scales, and 6 conditions.
H1, H7, and H8 account for ${>}90\%$ of hacking; H7 includes obfuscated subtype H7b ($14/350$) that evades text-match classifiers (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).
ISR modestly increases H7 convergence probability ($\text{OR}{=}2.84$, $p{<}5{\times}10^{-12}$, 5-seed; Appendix Table~\ref{tab:bootstrap-ci}), but per-seed variance dominates (Random s46: $91.5\%$ H7; ISR s46: $14.3\%$).
All GRPO conditions show ${\geq}80\%$ pooled hacking; only SFT achieves $92.3\%$ non-hacking.
Cochran--Mantel--Haenszel tests stratified by seed confirm both effects (H7: $\text{OR}_{\text{CMH}}{=}2.46$, $p{<}10^{-15}$; genuine: $\text{OR}_{\text{CMH}}{=}3.37$, $p{<}10^{-9}$), indicating that the associations are robust to within-seed clustering.

\section{Discussion and Conclusion}
\label{sec:discussion}

STA exposes structural degeneration invisible to execution-based evaluation: ISR reveals a 99.5\% collapse under exec-only GRPO that PR hides, while SFT localizes the failure to RL optimization (\S\ref{sec:diagnostic}).
Repurposed as a training signal, ISR exhibits Goodhart collapse observed at all four tested doses ($\beta\in\{0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3\}$): tautological proofs receive artificially high ISR (${\geq}0.5$ by construction), creating a positive feedback loop once sampled during rollouts.
The effect is consistent across logic types (Prolog: 0\% non-hacking, 3/3 seeds), model scales (1.7B: novel gaming modes), and training durations (500$\to$1000 steps).
At 500 steps, ISR increases the proportion of genuine proofs relative to random controls ($22.6\%$ vs.\ $7.7\%$; $\text{OR}{=}3.48$, uncorrected); under stricter H8+FN-corrected classification (3-seed subset), OR reduces to $0.61$ (n.s.), and extended training on both seeds~42 and~45 (1000 steps) confirms the genuine window closes (s42: $17\%{\to}2\%$; s45: $55\%{\to}0\%$).
ISR is reliable as a diagnostic but unreliable as an optimizer: the same LOO bias that rewards genuine necessity also rewards tautological constructions.

\paragraph{Practical implications.}
$\beta$ controls the \emph{timing} of collapse, not whether it occurs (\S\ref{sec:goodhart}); snapshot evaluation overestimates ISR's benefit.
Text-match classifiers have systematic blind spots (H7b, query-as-fact, H9 all evade detection); mandatory functional cross-validation is needed (\S\ref{sec:taxonomy}).
Different model capacities converge to different exploits (\S\ref{sec:crossscale}); no safe scale was observed in our single-seed evaluation (\S\ref{sec:limitations}).
ISR and similar perturbation-based metrics should serve as post-hoc evaluation tools, not training signals.
Future work should explore ISR variants that penalize tautological constructions and test generalization to other neurosymbolic domains beyond first-order logic.

Goodhart collapse~\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy} is observed at all four tested doses ($\beta{=}0.05$: 3 seeds; $\beta\in\{0.1, 0.2, 0.3\}$: 3--5 seeds each).
The structural bias predicts universality (H7 tautology is always the global reward-maximizing exploit regardless of $\beta$), and $\beta$ controls only the probability of early sampling and thus the timing of collapse; at $\beta{=}0.05$, three seeds confirm deterministic H7 collapse ($93.7\%$ pooled) while the matched random control at the same $\beta$ produces H1 redundancy instead ($77.4\%$), ruling out dose magnitude as the driver.
At moderate doses ($\beta{=}0.1$), collapse is stochastic and delayed (5 seeds bifurcate: 2 collapse rapidly, 3 sustain a transient genuine window that trajectory analysis confirms is temporary); at higher doses ($\beta{=}0.2$), collapse is immediate and universal.
$\beta{=}0.3$ adds reward collapse~\citep{gao-reward-overoptimization} as a competing failure mode (PR drops to 18\% in 1/3 seeds), but the underlying Goodhart vulnerability remains the same.
The practical implication is that ISR (and structurally similar LOO-based diagnostics) should be used exclusively as post-hoc evaluation tools, never as training rewards.

\paragraph{Single-seed unreliability.}
The three exec-only seeds diverge radically (PR $\sigma{=}47$ percentage points), each converging to a qualitatively different degeneration mode (\S\ref{sec:diagnostic}).
ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ (5 seeds) shows even greater instability: 2/5 seeds collapse to H7 within ${\sim}150$ steps, while 3/5 sustain a transient genuine window.
The 5-seed pooled non-hacking rate is ${\sim}23\%$ at 500 steps; trajectory analysis on seeds~42 and~45 (1000 steps) confirms this is temporary ($17\%{\to}2\%$ and $55\%{\to}0\%$ genuine respectively).
The dominant hacking mode (H7 vs.\ H1) is stochastic within any treatment condition ($\text{CV}{>}1$).
Multi-seed evaluation with trajectory analysis should be standard practice for neurosymbolic RL systems; single-seed or single-checkpoint results can misrepresent a configuration's true hacking profile.
